### Historical audit

**Source:** S0034, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/selection/commons_135156253/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 5 is visible; cited offsets cover the supplied observations.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Line 12, student `model_request`, characters [0,218874) | The instruction was to reconstruct a 512 × 341 reference with separate meshes and matching camera. The student’s code interpreted it as a garden bistro: one round table, two folding chairs, lawn and hedge. This scene interpretation is inferred from code, not independently verified against the unavailable image. |
| Line 12, same observation | The first build failed at `world.use_nodes` because the scene world was `None`. The student supplied a complete revision that creates and assigns a world if missing. Step 2 reported `ok: true` and a saved render. That establishes technical execution, not visual or geometric fidelity. |
| Lines 14–15, student `model_response` and step 3 `execute`, characters [0,10795) and [0,11431) | After the step 2 render was supplied, the student revised and launched a third build. It moved and raised the table, changed chair positions, rotations and one width, lowered the camera and changed its lens, altered lighting, perforations and lawn/hedge detail, and added small flowers. No step 3 result is visible. |
| Line 13, student `codex_session`, characters [0,3327) | The reference and step 2 render were supplied to a fresh read-only session; it completed with zero tool calls. The visible revision is autonomous in this session, but the trace does not expose its visual reasoning. No teacher message, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is visible in this chunk. |

**Scene checks and uncertainty.** The code specifies multiple objects, painted-metal panels, procedural ground and foliage materials, crossed legs, rails, seat supports and curved chair backs. These are modeled components and intended connections; neither physical joining nor correct pose, occlusion, material appearance, camera framing or lighting match is verified. The first failure was a concrete render setup error; step 2 recovered technically. The student requested 48 Cycles samples, while the step 2 log shows 16, so actual runner settings may differ from program settings.

**Outcome and lessons.** This is a nonempty, iterated patch with a reported successful intermediate render and an initially interrupted build; overall reconstruction correctness and final outcome remain **unknown**. A transferable observation is that handling a missing Blender world allowed the next execution to succeed. The furniture dimensions, procedural vegetation and camera choices are task-specific attempts, not validated general solutions. Whether step 3 improved the image, connected parts convincingly, or completed successfully remains unresolved; neither referenced image is visible to this audit.
